blocks.content: THE PREAMBLE OF THE INDIAN CONSTITUTION

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The idea of the Preamble was borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America.
The Preamble originated from the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added three new words: Socialist, Secular, and Integrity.
The Supreme Court affirmed that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and forms part of its Basic Structure in the Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973).
India practices Democratic Socialism and ensures state neutrality toward all religions.

blocks.content: The Preamble is the introductory part of the Indian Constitution. It reflects the philosophy, ideals, objectives and spirit of the Constitution. The Preamble acts as the guiding light for understanding the Constitution and its provisions.
The Preamble begins with the famous words:
„WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA…‟
It shows that the ultimate sovereignty lies with the people of India.
HISTORICAL BACKGROUND OF THE PREAMBLE
The idea of the Preamble was borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America.
The objectives of the Indian Constitution were first laid down in the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946.
The Objectives Resolution later became the Preamble of the Constitution.
TEXT OF THE PREAMBLE
WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens:
JUSTICE – social, economic and political;
LIBERTY – of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; EQUALITY – of status and of opportunity;
and to promote among them all
FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation;
IN OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this 26th day of November, 1949, do HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION.
KEY WORDS OF THE PREAMBLE
The Preamble contains important keywords that define the nature of the Indian State.
SOVEREIGN
Sovereign means that India is independent and not subject to any external authority. India can make its own laws and conduct its internal and external affairs freely.
SOCIALIST
The word „Socialist‟ was added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. It means:
India follows Democratic Socialism, not State Socialism.
The Preamble is the soul of the Indian Constitution.
SECULAR
The word „Secular‟ was also added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976. India does not have any state religion.
The State treats all religions equally and does not discriminate on religious grounds.
DEMOCRATIC
Democratic means government of the people, by the people and for the people. India follows:
REPUBLIC
Republic means that the head of the State is elected and not a hereditary ruler.
The President of India is elected for a fixed term of five years.

PREAMBLE AND SUPREME COURT JUDGMENTS

CONCLUSION

The Preamble is the soul of the Indian Constitution. It reflects the dreams and aspirations of the people of India. It acts as a guiding star for the Constitution and ensures that India remains a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic committed to justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
